items.q: Bilateral woody submandibular swelling, floor of mouth raised, tongue pushed up, drooling after molar pain defines what?
items.exp: Ludwig angina is bilateral submandibular cellulitis (odontogenic) elevating tongue toward airway obstruction; it is primarily cellulitis though drainage and tooth removal plus airway control treat it.
r: Incorrect. Quinsy is unilateral peritonsillar.
Correct. Ludwig angina floor of mouth emergency.
Incorrect. Parotid swells cheek preauricular.
Incorrect. Ranula is cystic floor swelling chronic.
items.kp: Woody mouth floor equals Ludwig airway alert.

items.q: First action in Ludwig angina with worsening drooling and voice change is what?
o: Airway securing plan in theatre or ICU setting with ENT anaesthesia, anticipating tracheostomy
items.exp: Progressive floor swelling obstructs unpredictably; controlled airway (often awake fibreoptic or tracheostomy under local) precedes transport or drainage. Blind intubation attempts can lose airway.
r: Incorrect. Scanner trip without airway risks arrest.
Correct. Secure airway in controlled setting first.
Incorrect. Discharge unsafe.
Incorrect. Drainage follows airway control.

items.q: Teenager recovers from sore throat then develops fever, lateral neck pain, rigors and lung septic emboli. Syndrome and organism?
o: Lemierre syndrome; Fusobacterium necrophorum jugular thrombophlebitis
items.exp: Lemierre follows oropharyngeal infection (often Fusobacterium necrophorum) infecting internal jugular clot showering lungs; needs prolonged antibiotics, imaging and anticoagulation debate in specialist care.
r: Correct. Lemierre Fusobacterium jugular sepsis.
Incorrect. Quinsy localises peritonsillar without emboli.
Incorrect. EBV lacks septic emboli pattern.
Incorrect. Fungus not classic agent.
items.kp: Sore throat, then neck, then lungs: Lemierre.

items.q: Retropharyngeal abscess in a 3 year old most closely mimics which conditions in presentation?
o: Epiglottitis and meningitis (fever, drooling, neck stiffness or extension avoidance)
items.exp: Prevertebral swelling causes fever, drooling, stridor and neck held stiff or extended, overlapping epiglottitis airway and meningitis stiffness; lateral neck imaging or CT after airway safety separates them.
r: Incorrect. Croup barks with steeple, less stiffness.
Correct. Epiglottitis and meningitis mimicry.
Incorrect. Asthma wheezes lower airway.
Incorrect. Foreign body is one cause in adults pattern.
items.kp: Stiff drooling toddler: pus behind throat hides.

items.q: Small sentinel bleed from neck wound days after parapharyngeal abscess warns of what catastrophe?
items.exp: Infected carotid sheath can erode arterial wall; herald bleeds precede exsanguinating blowout needing immediate theatre vascular control, airway and massive transfusion activation.
r: Incorrect. Jugular clot embolises, not sentinel bleed.
Correct. Carotid blowout herald bleed.
Incorrect. Fistula leaks saliva, not arterial warning.
Incorrect. Tracheitis inflames airway without this sign.
items.kp: Warning bleed from infected neck: carotid next.

items.q: Descending necrotising mediastinitis from neck infection requires which team addition and why?
o: Cardiothoracic surgery; mediastinal drainage beyond neck access
items.exp: Pus descending retropharyngeal or pretracheal planes into mediastinum cannot clear by neck incisions alone; thoracic drainage, broad sepsis care and repeat imaging drive survival.
r: Incorrect. Skin not central issue.
Correct. Thoracic drainage needed.
Incorrect. Eyes uninvolved pathway.
Incorrect. Dental source removal necessary but insufficient.
items.kp: Neck pus in chest needs chest surgeons.

items.q: Pain out of proportion, bronze bullae, crepitus and rapid spread in diabetic neck infection indicate what until disproven?
o: Necrotising fasciitis needing immediate surgical debridement
items.exp: Necrotising soft tissue infection outruns antibiotics; early wide excision to healthy tissue with ICU and broad cover is life and airway saving, imaging must not delay theatre in classic signs.
r: Incorrect. Simple cellulitis lacks necrosis signs.
Correct. Necrotising fasciitis, debride now.
Incorrect. Allergy itches without crepitus pain.
Incorrect. Stone obstructs gland mealtimes.
items.kp: Crepitus plus agony equals theatre, not observation.

items.q: Commonest source overall for deep neck space infections in adults is what?
items.exp: Lower molar roots below mylohyoid line seed submandibular and related spaces; dental imaging and extraction are source control without which antibiotics and drainage relapse.
r: Incorrect. Sinuses infect orbit and brain more.
Correct. Teeth lead adult deep neck sepsis.
Incorrect. Ear infects mastoid pathways.
Incorrect. Skin is minority source.

items.q: Stable airway child suspected retropharyngeal abscess: preferred imaging to confirm and plan?
o: Contrast CT neck (after airway assessment), lateral soft tissue film adjunct historically
items.exp: CT defines retropharyngeal collection, mediastinal extent and drainage route in stable children; unstable airway bypasses imaging to theatre. Plain lateral widening supports but lacks surgical detail.
r: Incorrect. Confirmation and extent needed.
Correct. Contrast CT when airway stable.
Incorrect. Spine MRI suits vertebral cause later.
Incorrect. Teeth ultrasound irrelevant.
items.kp: Stable: CT maps pus before drainage.

items.q: Ludwig angina microbiology and cover pattern typically target what?
o: Polymicrobial oral flora: streptococci plus anaerobes (staphylococci by setting)
items.exp: Oral polymicrobial synergy drives cellulitis, so empirical regimens cover streptococci and anaerobes per local policy, narrowed by operative cultures, with MRSA additions by risk.
r: Incorrect. Viruses do not cause Ludwig.
Correct. Mixed oral aerobes and anaerobes.
Incorrect. Pseudomonas is ear canal pattern.
Incorrect. Antifungals only immunocompromised proof.
items.kp: Mouth pus is mixed: cover anaerobes too.
